description.html: This mask looks like an object excavated from an ancient temple. The dark, gray-brown surface has the texture of weathered stone, and finely engraved swirling patterns intertwine across the forehead and cheeks. The face is elongated, with a pronounced nose and lips and two large eye holes.

The mask is curved and has an arched opening on its lower edge, so when it is laid over the substrate it leaves a sheltered space underneath that a small animal can crawl into. Leaned upright against a stone or the back wall, it looks like a relief from a ruin. It fits desert and tropical terrariums, and especially themed setups with skulls and Aztec motifs.

When using it as a hide, press it slightly into the substrate so it does not move, and check that the openings are not so narrow that the animal could get stuck in them. To clean it, take it out, rinse it with lukewarm water without detergent and go over the engraved patterns with a soft brush, then let it dry completely before putting it back in the terrarium.
